title: WEDM Tier 6 — Spline Broach + PCD Tooling
philosophy: WC carbide spline broach and PCD inserts are the two hardest tool-material pairs for WEDM. PCD requires thermal-conductivity k(T) interpolation — NOT Johnson-Cook (which is plasticity).

formulas: modified thermal-conductivity k(T) interpolation for PCD per ASM Handbook Vol. 16 p. 317
anisotropic k for PCD via diamond-Co composite rule-of-mixtures (Field 1992)
reference: ASM Handbook Vol. 16 Machining for PCD k(T)
Field 1992 Properties of Natural and Synthetic Diamond

units.title: Spline broach (internal involute, WC carbide, tight OD tolerance)
units.loop: BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP
exit_criteria: G-code contains structural tokens G41/G42, M00/M01, wire-thread markers
units.description: Spline broach (internal involute, WC carbide, tight OD tolerance) — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: PCD tooling (polycrystalline diamond inserts, k(T) interpolation)
units.loop: BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP
abort_conditions: PCD path returns conductivity via Johnson-Cook (wedm-pcd-conductivity-gate blocks)
k(T) interpolator deviates > ±5% from ASM tabulated values
exit_criteria_additional: PCD k(T) interpolator returns within ±5% of ASM published values at 300-1200 K
